races.name: Power Utilities Group Conditional Jockeys' Selling Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Pigeon House
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner here, Beau Morgan takes the ride for the Pogsons; recent course form over 16f on Good ground is positive and headgear (p) suggests he switches on well — uncontested lead at 2m2½f on this surface is a significant asset.
runners_data.comment: Ran well for second two starts back, and a winner four starts back, but his two pulled ups either side of those efforts demand respect as a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 49 days between runs leaves fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: At The Oche
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's yard is firing (T14: 9/27) and Harry Atkins claims 3lb on a horse whose form string reads 222-1B — four place efforts before a recent win, with strong sim-going figures (9/11); the prominent style suits a race where the pace is controlled and he can simply travel into contention.
runners_data.comment: Placed on four of his last five starts with a win one start back and a string of seconds before that, At The Oche arrives fit on a 13-day turnaround with distance and going experience to call upon; the concern is that being brought down last time needs forgetting.

runners_data.name: Mountain Port
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse in a race with several rivals sharing that tendency, so he will be deeper than ideal; the form string /770-0 flags a horse struggling for consistency and the 'fades in finish' warning is a real concern at this trip on Good ground — 64 days off adds further uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Mountain Port has run over today's going before and returns after a 64-day break that could have him freshened up nicely, while 152 lb is a stiff ask for a gelding yet to win in his last four starts.

runners_data.name: Versatile
runners_data.note: Has raced frequently (9 days since last run) and his hold-up profile means he faces the same positional squeeze as the redistributed horses; sim-going figures (7/15 without a win) do not inspire confidence, though his consistency around 16f on Good suggests he will finish off his race without threatening.
runners_data.comment: Versatile has been consistently placed in the frame without troubling the judge, and his 4th last time out — just nine days ago — keeps him fit, though winless in his last five starts and our rating of 90 suggests he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Mojo Ego
runners_data.note: Fergal O'Brien's runner has genuine hold-up credentials but the field density at the rear means he will end up racing out of his preferred position — his style-fit score of 0.93 signals a meaningful discount; the one win in his recent form came from tracking closer, so mid-group may not be entirely alien, but this race shape does not set up for him.
runners_data.comment: Mojo Ego shaped with some promise when third last time out, but sixth two starts back and ranked sixth of seven on our figures make him hard to fancy at 145 lb, even if he has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Raffles Nobu
runners_data.note: Jack Stenhouse's 5lb claim helps offset a modest OR of 89 on a horse whose sim-going record (9/15, 1W5P) is solid and whose consistent recent form (421353) shows he finds the frame regularly; a prominent runner with headgear (tb) who should travel sweetly behind Pigeon House and be competitive deep into the straight.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying 142 lb, Raffles Nobu is hard to fancy despite some placing in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a win four starts back shows he can find the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's runner is a genuine hold-up type at heart — 48 days since last run and a form string of -039PP raises serious questions about jumping and commitment; the style-fit discount (0.91) reflects that he will not be racing where he is most effective, and there is little in recent evidence to suggest he can overcome that disadvantage here.
runners_data.comment: Chillhi has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 102 suggests he holds solid claims at an official mark of 88, making him a genuine threat here; however, two consecutive pulled-up efforts are an obvious concern that connections will need to explain away.

races.paceDynamic: Pigeon House is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will control tempo from the outset at a pace of his own choosing — likely steady to moderate on Good ground over 2m2½f. At The Oche and Raffles Nobu will press forward to track him prominently, creating a compact, well-ordered gallop rather than a burn-up, which means the pace is sustainable and unlikely to collapse catastrophically for the leaders. Mojo Ego and Chillhi are genuine hold-up horses by nature but the preponderance of rear-dwellers in this small field means both have been mapped into midfield; in practice they will be unable to take their preferred pitch at the back and the track position they occupy will be somewhat forced rather than chosen. This controlled, single-pacemaker shape strongly favours horses racing prominently — Pigeon House dictating and At The Oche or Raffles Nobu stalking within striking range — because the pace will not be fierce enough to set the race up for a late challenge from horses who need a stronger gallop to generate momentum.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pigeon House Controls, Prominent Pair Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Pigeon House leads unchallenged and At The Oche and Raffles Nobu track closely throughout.
scenarios.body: Pigeon House dictates a measured pace, keeping the field in a tight bunch and giving nothing away; when the tempo lifts from three out, At The Oche and Raffles Nobu are ideally positioned to mount their challenges on the front-runner. This shape overwhelmingly suits horses racing in the first three, rewarding race-reading over raw finishing speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pigeon House Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is even more sedate than expected and Pigeon House is simply never headed.
scenarios.body: A slow crawl through the early stages means Pigeon House bowls along on the front end barely asked a question, and no rival travelling strongly enough in behind can sustain the effort to reel him in at the business end. This scenario suits a front-runner who controls every variable — Pigeon House's recent course form and positive headgear record make him the natural beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Movers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves surprisingly hot early and leaders tie up in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Should a tempo miscalculation from Pigeon House or pressure from Raffles Nobu create a genuine gallop, the horses shuffled into midfield — Mojo Ego and Versatile — could find energy reserves the leaders have spent. However, both Mojo Ego and Chillhi carry a style-fit discount here because they are not racing in their true hold-up role and may lack the genuine finishing kick this scenario demands from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fallers/Chaos Shake Up
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors or early incidents disrupt the anticipated race shape and reshuffle positions mid-race.
scenarios.body: A horse-jumping incident that unseats or significantly hampers the pace-setter would suddenly produce a riderless or leaderless scenario, opening the door to an opportunist scramble. Mountain Port, who has shown the ability to stay on honestly in similar going even if his finishing effort fades, could capitalise if he avoids trouble and finds himself in an unexpectedly forward berth.

watchPoints.text: Pigeon House sets an uncontested but very slow early gallop — watch whether At The Oche or Raffles Nobu elect to press him, because if neither does, the race becomes a sprint finish that could catch out the true hold-up runners entirely.

Mojo Ego and Chillhi are both natural rear-dwellers forced to race in a more prominent position than they prefer — watch their early jumping and energy expenditure, as racing out of role over hurdles in a small field can lead to jumping errors when horses are unsettled by their position.

Mountain Port's 64-day absence and declining form string (/770-0) make him a horse to monitor at the first few hurdles — a jumping lapse early would confirm he is not at his best and remove him from any calculation.

At The Oche ran just 13 days ago but the Skelton yard's current strike rate (9/27 over 14 days) means quick returns are routine and planned — watch his early manoeuvre to assess whether Harry Atkins elects to sit just off Pigeon House or drops in behind Raffles Nobu.

Raffles Nobu's headgear (tb) typically sharpens focus through the early exchanges — watch whether Jack Stenhouse uses the 5lb claim to place him aggressively in second or third early, as that position is where this scenario's value is concentrated.

races.name: What The Frunk: The Geely Ex2 Novices' Hurdle Race (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Gambino
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's five-year-old has solid course-applicable form (wins at 17f Good) and Harry Skelton in the saddle is a major positive, but with Pioneer Pete and Tazman Dan also in the race, he's unlikely to claim his natural prominent berth and will find himself racing further back than ideal — temper expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: King's Scholar
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old boasts the highest OR at 123 and a strong good-ground winning profile (two wins at 16f Good), though 100 days off and a claim jockey (Tom Hutsby, 10lb) introduce slight uncertainties; a prominent racing style suits this honest gallop well and he looks the main tracking danger.

runners_data.name: Pioneer Pete
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with an excellent similar-going strike rate (8/9, two wins at 16f Good) and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. in the saddle; after 91 days off he returns to good ground which he handles well, and dictating from the front at Stratford's flat track plays to every strength he has.

runners_data.name: Tazman Dan
runners_data.note: Stuart Edmunds sends him out after a lengthy 153-day break and his recent form (657) is uninspiring; while he is a genuine front-runner who will challenge Pioneer Pete for the lead, his light similar-going record (1/3, no wins) and return from absence mean he is more likely to compromise the pace than control it.

runners_data.name: Bailey's Luck
runners_data.note: Clare Hobson's four-year-old is flagged as a hold-up type who fades in the finish — a damaging combination in a race likely to be run at an honest clip; 43 days since last run is fine, but the form reads P0 and the headgear entry over a longer trip does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Don't Rein Me In
runners_data.note: Chris Honour's lightly-raced four-year-old ran a reasonable second at 13f on good ground and holds a prominent style that suits this pace scenario, but has been off 167 days and Bryan Carver takes over with no trainer-14-day winners to boost confidence; the step up to 2m½f is also uncharted territory.

runners_data.name: Northwest Passage
runners_data.note: Ivan Furtado's four-year-old was placed at 10f Good but is stepping up dramatically in trip to 2m½f and holds a poor similar-going record (0/7 wins); a 5lb claimer in William Shanahan and a lack of any win at distances remotely comparable make this a significant ask on paper.

races.paceDynamic: Pioneer Pete and Tazman Dan are both confirmed front-runners, and their presence together guarantees a contested, honest gallop from the off at Stratford over 2m½f on good ground. Pioneer Pete holds the stronger form at pace (8/9 similar-going record with two wins), while Tazman Dan's recent form reads 657 and brings more questions than answers after 153 days off, meaning Pioneer Pete is the likelier pace controller if a duel doesn't materialise. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions — Gambino is a genuine prominent racer who will find himself shuffled wider into midfield, with King's Scholar and Don't Rein Me In the prominent types most likely to actually claim that early rail berth behind the leaders. An honest, competitive gallop over this flat Stratford configuration on quick ground suits horses who travel prominently with fluency and can sustain their effort late — closers will need an honest enough pace to reel the leaders back, but the dominant shape favours those racing prominently behind a genuine front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pioneer Pete Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pioneer Pete establishes clean lead and Tazman Dan doesn't sustain a duel past halfway, creating a true-pace gallop that rewards the prominent brigade.
scenarios.body: Pioneer Pete has the superior good-ground record at this trip (8/9 sim-going, two wins) and Jonjo O'Neill Jr. will press for an uncontested lead early; at Stratford's flat, turning track this rewards horses who jump fluently and sustain a strong rhythm throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Tazman Dan forces a genuine duel with Pioneer Pete that burns them both out, leaving prominent-tracking types to sweep past the tiring leaders in the final flight.
scenarios.body: A true pace battle between the two front-runners at an honest clip would cause both to weaken on the run-in, handing the race to whichever prominent horse has settled just off the pace and jumped cleanly throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tazman Dan Upsets at Big Price
scenarios.trigger: If Tazman Dan, returned after 153 days, finds peak fitness and his rider controls the pace solo rather than being challenged, settling into a comfortable lead.
scenarios.body: Stuart Edmunds does target seasonal return winners and if Tazman Dan is cherry-ripe, an uncontested lead could see him produce a career-best over this trip in better ground than he's tackled; his sim-going record is thin (1/3) so this remains a low-probability outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Field In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace burns ferociously throughout and the prominent runners are also compromised, giving Bailey's Luck or Gambino a late finishing run.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends on Gambino and Bailey's Luck operating from their natural prominent positions, but Gambino is redistributed out of role into midfield and Bailey's Luck carries a fade-in-finish flag, making both less reliable as genuine closers; this shape requires everything to go wrong up front simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Pioneer Pete vs Tazman Dan — watch the first half-mile closely; if Tazman Dan pushes Pioneer Pete into a lung-busting duel rather than yielding, both front-runners could capitulate, changing the complexion of the race entirely.

Gambino — Harry Skelton may attempt to push forward aggressively from the break to reclaim his natural prominent position, potentially crowding King's Scholar or Don't Rein Me In in the early stages; watch for traffic complications near the front.

King's Scholar — 100 days off and a conditional jockey means there is fitness and partnership uncertainty; if Tom Hutsby struggles to hold a prominent position through the early hurdles, his chance could evaporate before the race truly begins.

Bailey's Luck — flagged fader who has finished outside the frame in both recent runs including a pulled-up; if she's struggling jumping the last bend, watch for a possible easing by Ben Poste rather than being hard-ridden to a poor finish.

Northwest Passage — a dramatic trip extension from his form distances (10-12f) to 2m½f; if he's clearly laboring before the third-last, it signals the step up is too sharp and he can be discounted from any scenario involving a late finish.

races.name: Allan Atkinson Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Jet Patrol
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid recent form in similar conditions (sim-going 11/15, 2 wins), Sean Bowen takes the mount which is a positive booking for a 9-year-old who handles good ground reliably; 16 days since last run is fine and this trip suits his profile well.
runners_data.comment: Jet Patrol shaped with real promise when second last time out, and having run over today's distance and going he arrives with strong claims; the main risk is that he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Langton Wold
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse dropping back in trip from a recent run on good ground; Nathan Moscrop rides for out-of-form Brian Ellison (T14: 2/21), and his all-turf good-ground profile (10/15 sim-going) is a positive, though finding a late run in this pace-dominated race will require patience and a clean run through.
runners_data.comment: Langton Wold has been a model of consistency, finishing second twice and third once in his last three starts, and he returns on a quick 12-day turnaround having already run over today's distance and going. Yet to score in recent starts, and a trainer in lean form gives slight pause, but his 104 rating heads the field.

runners_data.name: Mayday Games
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over course-and-distance conditions earlier this season; Brendan Powell navigates a difficult assignment because he must lead but will have Genbu and Saucats alongside him — the moderate trainer strike rate (T14: 1/2) in recent days is a minor positive, and this horse's stamina on good ground is proven over 16f.
runners_data.comment: Mayday Games arrives here on the back of a third last time out in good heart, and a winner three starts back gives his recent form a solid foundation; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 163 lb the weight is the chief query.

runners_data.name: Lord Of The Glance
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with strong placed form (21U-23 recent) over this distance and surface; 7-year-old with a genuine good-ground profile (sim-going 6/12, 1W3P) and the 3lb claimer Toby McCain-Mitchell reducing the weight burden slightly — one of the more credible profiles to run into the prize if the pace collapses.
runners_data.comment: Lord Of The Glance has placed third last time out and was a winner four starts back, though an unseating rider three starts back interrupts what is otherwise a consistent recent profile; he has run over today's trip and going, but 159 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Western Soldier
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse returning after 67 days off for Jeff Mullins; the amateur jockey Benjamin Macey (5lb claim) on a horse with modest recent form (9U-45P) after a layoff is a concern, and while his good-ground record is adequate, the absence and the competitive pace scenario make him a risky proposition.
runners_data.comment: Western Soldier has run over today's trip and going, our rating of 92 puts him right among the leading players, and 157 lb is a manageable burden for a gelding of his profile; the concern is that he is winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up latest.

runners_data.name: Connemara Joe
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose natural instinct is to race at the rear — in this field loaded with hold-up types, he is likely to end up closer to midfield than he would prefer; his going stats on good are a perfect 4/4 for sim-going encounters, and Matt Sheppard's runner 13 days fresh is a workable return, but his OR of 82 and a 0W0P record from the back mark him as a big ask at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up among his recent finishes and a rating of 78 ranking him ninth of ten on our figures, Connemara Joe faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's distance and going and returns on a relatively quick turnaround of 13 days.

runners_data.name: Genbu
runners_data.note: Front-runner carrying an amateur rider (Mr Sam Burton, 7lb claim) and with a form string of 33548U that raises stamina doubts over this trip; his good-ground sim-going record is decent (10/15, 1W5P), but a four-year-old contesting a pace war against more seasoned front-runners looks a tough assignment, and the U (unseated) on his most recent run is a jumping concern.
runners_data.comment: Genbu arrives on the back of an unseating last time out, though he showed fair form before that with a third five starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going; yet to win in recent starts and a 153 lb burden makes life harder.

runners_data.name: Saucats
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with the most consistent course profile of the front trio — five consecutive runs over 18f on good, including 1-2-3 placed efforts; Callum Pritchard partners a horse in headgear (tp) who knows how to compete up front, and at OR 81 carrying 152lbs, he will be competitive if the pace is within his control, which it likely will not be entirely given Mayday Games and Genbu's presence.
runners_data.comment: Ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Saucats is hard to fancy off 152 lb, and a seventh last time out does little to inspire confidence; the consolation is a win four starts back and experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Battle Stride
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a significant concern in a stamina-testing pace-heavy race; his true hold-up style means he is unlikely to secure his preferred position with three other confirmed rearward horses in the field — Philip Armson (3lb claim) on a 52-day returner with a poor sim-going record (4/11, 0W0P) and a form string including a fall makes this an unappealing profile.
runners_data.comment: Battle Stride is winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, making him very hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 52 days with fitness perhaps restored.

runners_data.name: Raincloud
runners_data.note: Returning after 105 days off — the longest layoff in the field — for Michael Chapman, who has had no runners in the last 14 days; Raincloud's recent form (99P8-8) and his preference for longer trips (20-23f in history) both raise serious doubts over 2m½f, and as a true hold-up horse in a race already crowded at the rear, finding room and producing a finishing effort looks extremely difficult.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and pulled up three runs back, Raincloud arrives after a 105-day break carrying 142 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and our rating of 81 suggests more ability than her official mark of 68 implies.

races.paceDynamic: Mayday Games, Genbu, and Saucats are all confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead over 2m½f on good ground at Stratford, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset that will test stamina throughout. These three will fight for position in the first half-mile, meaning no single horse dictates a comfortable solo lead — the pace is likely to be genuine and unrelenting rather than manufactured. This race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently without expending energy in the early battle, or patient hold-up horses with a serious finishing kick — provided those hold-up types can genuinely settle and produce late runs. However, Connemara Joe, Battle Stride, and Raincloud are true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield because the field contains more horses seeking the rear than the race shape can accommodate cleanly; of those three, Connemara Joe is most likely to find something resembling a workable position given his youth and handler record on this going, while Battle Stride's fade tendency makes him the least likely to capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Suits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out and a prominent, economical tracker pounces from second or third.
scenarios.body: Mayday Games, Genbu, and Saucats push hard early and the pace unravels the front trio entering the final circuit, opening the door for a horse that has tracked without over-committing; the stamina demands on good ground over this trip will catch those who led from the outset.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Test
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace-setters settles fractionally better than the others and conserves enough to hold on from the front.
scenarios.body: Saucats, who has course experience over similar trips and recorded form figures of 1-2-3 over 18f on good, is best placed among the speed horses to dictate a controlled enough rhythm to stay on; Mayday Games also holds this possibility having won over the distance on this going, though the multi-way pace battle makes front-running survival harder than a lone leader scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace war between the front trio is truly combustible, creating a strong enough collapse to allow a genuine hold-up horse to sweep through late.
scenarios.body: Lord Of The Glance and Langton Wold are the most credible closers in the field with legitimate hold-up profiles and recent form showing placed efforts on good ground; however, the redistributed hold-up types (Connemara Joe, Battle Stride, Raincloud) are less likely to reach their natural late position in a congested rear, reducing the depth of the closing challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If multiple fallers or interference in the scrappy early pace battle disrupts the race shape entirely, producing a chaotic finish.
scenarios.body: A contested three-way lead duel over hurdles raises the risk of crowding or jumping errors that reshuffle the field unpredictably; in such a scenario, horses with reliable jumping and stamina reserves at a fair weight would hold an edge.

watchPoints.text: Mayday Games, Genbu, and Saucats — watch the first two furlongs for a three-way lead duel that could set a brutal gallop and compromise all three horses' finishing ability.
Genbu — his most recent run ended in an unseat, and competing for the lead over hurdles after a jumping mishap is a material risk to race safety and the shape of the contest.
Raincloud — 105 days off with no recent trainer runners and step down in trip makes him a potential fader or non-stayer who could cause interference in the closing stages.

Lord Of The Glance — watch whether Toby McCain-Mitchell settles him conservatively in the early chaos; if he gets a clean position tracking the pace in fourth or fifth, his closing form (21U-23) makes him a live player.

Battle Stride — flagged for finishing weakness and carrying a hold-up style into a crowded rear; if he gets shuffled too far back in the early pace scramble, he is unlikely to reach a competitive position before the race is won.

races.name: Wynchwood Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Breaking Cover
runners_data.note: Top-weighted hold-up horse dropping to 2m1f from further trips where he has finished well; Chad Bament's 5lb claim is useful, the 4W7P record on Good ground is strong, and coming here fresh on 9 days' rest for Honeyball suits; structurally gifted by three pace-horses ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: Breaking Cover comes here in good heart, a winner last time out just nine days ago and carrying that fitness boost into today, with experience of both the trip and the going working in his favour. The weight of 168 lb is the one factor to keep an eye on.

runners_data.name: Captain Cool
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish has one winner from twelve in the past 14 days but this horse is in career form — 122131 — and his 13/15 Good-going record over similar distances is outstanding; Sean Quinlan can park him prominently just off the war and his class at OR 131 gives him the widest margin for error.
runners_data.comment: Captain Cool arrives in cracking heart, a winner last time out and a third two starts back sandwiched between victories, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the weight burden of 164 lb is the one factor his supporters must hope he handles.

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner with a 41-day absence and a form string featuring two pulled-ups and no wins in similar going; at OR 129 he has ability but the layoff and stamina question over 2m1f — having run mostly further — combined with sharing pace duties, makes him vulnerable late.
runners_data.comment: Third twice in recent starts and with experience of today's trip and conditions, Sony Bill holds strong claims at the top of our ratings, though connections will be eager to see him reproduce that form after a pulled-up effort last time out, winless in his last five.

runners_data.name: Sir Tivo
runners_data.note: A 12-year-old confirmed lead-seeker who gets Good ground well (12/15) and did win over 17f in that band, but his last run was a pulled-up and he's been competing through a long career; Sean Bowen is a quality booking that adds confidence, though having two rivals equally keen to lead will drain him.
runners_data.comment: Sir Tivo won two starts back and was third three starts back, and has run over today's distance and going before, and 16 days between runs leaves him fresh; the pullup last time is the obvious concern he must overcome.

runners_data.name: In This World
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who is naturally suited by this pace scenario but whose recent form includes a fall and a pulled-up, raising jumping reliability concerns; trainer B R Summers is 0/3 in the 14-day window and the 11-day turnaround is tight; Good ground form (11/15) is fair but he needs a clean round to factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a fall in the mix and two fifths alongside a pulled up, In This World faces a stiff ask ranked fifth of six on our figures, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 11 days.

runners_data.name: Gower Prince
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner with a 13/15 record on Good ground and two wins in that band, and a 21-day freshener could sharpen him; apprentice Benjamin Macey rides, which adds riding weight concerns in a contested pace scenario, but if either Sony Bill or Sir Tivo takes a back seat early, Gower Prince has the tactical speed to exploit and his 1-2-2 recent form shows he's competitive.
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures among six rivals, Gower Prince is hard to fancy despite a fair official mark of 108, though he arrives on the back of a win and a placed effort in his last two starts and has distance and going experience to call on.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill, Sir Tivo, and Gower Prince are all confirmed front-runners in a six-runner field, making a contested, fast-run gallop from the outset virtually certain over this 2m1f trip at Stratford on Good ground. At least one of the three will likely be squeezed for position early, but even if one or two are forced to settle slightly, the combined intent ensures a genuinely strong pace that will relentlessly test stamina into the home straight. The two hold-up horses, Breaking Cover and In This World, are handed a structural gift by this pace scenario — they can afford to race well off the speed, conserve energy over the fences, and produce their finishing effort when the leaders are crying enough. This race shape strongly favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles, as the front-runners will almost certainly burn each other out before the final two fences, leaving those ridden patiently best placed to swoop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Reign
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners set a genuinely punishing gallop that fractures their stamina in the final mile, allowing the hold-up horses to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Sony Bill, Sir Tivo, and Gower Prince trade blows up front throughout, and by the time they reach the final three fences at least one is already weakening; Breaking Cover and In This World, having been delivered fresh off the pace, find the most to give late. This is the statistically dominant shape given three genuine pace horses in a small field and suits the two hold-up profiles whose good ground form records are solid.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Captain Cool Bowls Up
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Cool, racing prominently, gets a dream run just off the contested pace and outstays everyone with his superior class and going record.
scenarios.body: Quinlan slots Captain Cool into a tracking role just behind the leading trio, letting them battle it out while he conserves energy, then produces a sustained challenge from two out that his 13/15 good-ground record strongly supports. At OR 131 he has the highest proven quality among those not front-running and his recent win-form — 122131 — marks him as a horse in excellent health.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace horses — most likely Gower Prince — gets an uncontested lead while the other two cancel each other out.
scenarios.body: Gower Prince, who won over this sort of trip on Good ground at OR 108 and has a 2W record in this going band, could exploit any early confusion between Sony Bill and Sir Tivo to slip clear and steal on the bridle; his handler Jonjo & A.J. O'Neill have the tactical nous for this even with an apprentice in the plate. If he builds a decisive advantage early and jumps fluently, the stronger-class hold-up horses may not have enough runway to reel him in.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Race, Chaos Plays
scenarios.trigger: If multiple jumping errors or fallers disrupt the pace and create an unpredictable stop-start gallop that nullifies the tactical advantage of the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: In This World, who has a fall and a pulled-up in recent form, is the obvious risk factor — any incident at a fence could bunch the field and produce a scrambled finish where positional riders and safer jumpers benefit. Sir Tivo at age 12 and Sony Bill with his pulled-up run also carry jumping uncertainty at pace, and a ragged middle section could allow a surviving front-runner to dictate on revised terms.

watchPoints.text: Watch for a speed duel between Sony Bill, Sir Tivo, and Gower Prince from the first fence — if all three insist on the lead the gallop will be extreme and their finishing effort will evaporate, gifting the race to the closers.

Gower Prince's apprentice jockey Benjamin Macey (5lb claim) may lack the authority to assert in a three-way front-running battle early; if outpaced at the start Gower Prince's whole race shape changes and he becomes a different threat.

In This World's jumping record — fall and pulled-up in recent form — is a live danger to race integrity in a small field; any incident at a fence involving him could interfere with the hold-up horses carrying most finishing expectation.

Captain Cool's last run was 16 days ago with a win over 20f on Good — the step back to 2m1f is the only distance query, but his 13/15 Going record means conditions are as good as they get for him and Quinlan will likely take the sit-and-deliver approach.

Breaking Cover's jockey Chad Bament claims 5lbs, effectively taking this horse down to a competitive mark; Anthony Honeyball's 2/8 14-day trainer strike rate is moderate but the horse's sim-going record (10/15, 4W7P) makes him one of the stronger empirical fits for today's conditions.

races.name: Rich Ellis's 60th Vinyl Countdown Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Roaring Home
runners_data.note: Strong prominent profile that has won at 2m over good ground and placed repeatedly at today's sort of trip; Sam Twiston-Davies is a powerful booking and 49 days off is not a concern given two recent wins fresh; a crisp jump at the final hurdles will be his key.
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Roaring Home faces a stiff task under 165 lb, and her two recent seconds suggest the winning thread has cooled, though she did score back-to-back three and four starts back and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Porter In The Park
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a solid record in similar going (13/15 runs) and two runs at 2m6f in recent history; Cameron Johnstone-Baker claims 7lb which softens the weight, though 94 days off is the obvious doubt and trainer Emma Lavelle's 0/6 in 14 days warns against over-commitment.
runners_data.comment: Porter In The Park shaped with plenty of promise when third and ninth in her two prior starts, and her experience over today's trip and going stands her in good stead; the main concern is that pulled-up run 94 days ago, leaving fitness on her comeback slightly in question.

runners_data.name: Jackstell
runners_data.note: Has form to a high level over shorter trips and the tongue-strap is re-applied today; Jamie Snowden is in decent form (1/11 over 14 days is modest but the yard fires runners fit), and while the step up to 2m6f is new territory, his four wins on good ground suggest conditions are fine.
runners_data.comment: Jackstell landed back-to-back wins in his last five starts and his experience on today's going is a clear asset at 162 lb; the main concern is a 67-day absence that leaves his current fitness an open question.

runners_data.name: Jaramillo
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator whose recent form reads 8-6-5-6 over 2m-2m3f trips, suggesting he needs things to go his way from the rear; Richard Upton's 10lb claim reduces his burden but trainer Warren Greatrex has been very active (4/13), so the horse is likely at his peak — trip is the opportunity, lack of pace cut is the risk.
runners_data.comment: Rated highest in this field and showing a third five starts back as his best recent effort, Jaramillo has experience over today's trip and going, though he arrives winless in his last five and must bounce back after a couple of modest efforts.

runners_data.name: Juan Bermudez
runners_data.note: Has two wins and strong placed efforts on good ground and handles shorter trips around 2m well; his natural style is to race prominently but the density of P-style horses in this field means he is likely to find himself further back than ideal, which tempers his chance in a shape where position behind the leader matters early.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and carrying a hefty 159 lb after 68 days off, Juan Bermudez is hard to fancy at face value, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and was a winner two starts back.

runners_data.name: Time To Bite
runners_data.note: Lone confirmed front-runner, 11 years old but has two wins at 2m6f on good going and went 1-2 in his last two runs at this trip; the blinkers help him concentrate and Bryan Carver's booking suits a hold-and-run job — his ability to set his own terms is the central structural fact of this race.
runners_data.comment: Time To Bite shaped with promise when second last time out and has run over today's trip and going, but an unplaced effort two starts back is a concern, and 48 days off the track leaves a fitness question ahead of this field.

runners_data.name: Notnowlinda
runners_data.note: Quick reappearance after just 16 days and a 4-4 double on good ground recently suggests Dan Skelton has her spot-on; Harry Skelton is a significant upgrade, but her hold-up profile means she needs the early gallop to be genuinely testing at 2m6f, and a dawdling Time To Bite could leave her with too much to find.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Notnowlinda does at least bring distance and going experience to the table and a third three starts back shows she can hit the frame, though carrying 156 lb looks a stiff ask for a mare rated 107 on official figures.

runners_data.name: Dinons
runners_data.note: Thirteen-year-old hold-up type who at his best on soft ground (four placed runs on soft or heavy) and rates a concern on today's good surface; Brian Ellison's 2/21 in 14 days is a tepid stat, and though he has been placed at 2m4f-2m6f, his true hold-up style and going preference make this a tough assignment from the map position assigned.
runners_data.comment: Dinons shaped with real promise when third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating of 115 puts him firmly in contention; the main concern is a trainer firing at just 5% in the last 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Time To Bite is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at 11 years old with a habit of front-running at this trip on good ground, will stride clear from the outset and attempt to control from the front without any genuine rival to apply pressure — Stratford's 2m6f at a steady pace suits a leader who can dictate on their own terms. Roaring Home, Porter In The Park, and Jackstell are all prominent types who will push for ground behind Time To Bite, meaning the early order will be competitive in the chasing pack even if the leader has daylight. Juan Bermudez is a natural prominent racer who cannot get that position in this field given the volume of P-style horses ahead of him, and Dinons — a genuine hold-up horse — has been pushed forward on the map for similar structural reasons; neither should be assumed to race from their mapped slot. This race shape — a lone leader setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop over a staying trip — strongly favours prominent chasers who can track economically and pick off a fading leader, rather than hold-up horses who must make ground from off a potentially dawdling early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Time To Bite is allowed to bowl along uncontested and sets a metronomic, sustainable gallop that saps the finishing kick of hold-up rivals.
scenarios.body: Time To Bite controls every yard, and the prominent chasers who track efficiently — rather than those covering extra ground from behind — are best placed to challenge as the leader either stays on or is reeled in close home; at 2m6f on good ground the stamina of those who race handy is rewarded.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Peg Back Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Home or Porter In The Park push up to pressure Time To Bite before the home turn, lifting the tempo and turning this into a true test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A stronger gallop stretches the field, and the horse who has settled best in the chasing position and jumps fluently at the final hurdles will grind out the finish; this shape exposes any hold-up horse who cannot get close enough to the pace to respond.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Time To Bite sets a genuine end-to-end gallop that empties the prominent horses, leaving a gap for a late-running type to come through.
scenarios.body: Notnowlinda or Jaramillo, racing from the rear, would need the gallop to be genuinely strong throughout to have enough momentum when they ask their questions from the home bend; this is structurally plausible but depends on a pace scenario that looks unlikely given Time To Bite's tendency to be economical rather than reckless.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Melee Behind Tiring Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Time To Bite fades after setting an honest pace and the prominent pack behind are also fatigued, leaving a scrambled, slow-motion finish.
scenarios.body: At 2m6f on good ground a muddled finish still tends to reward the horse with residual class or the freshest legs late; Notnowlinda, on a quick 16-day return, and Jaramillo, dropping in class on a good surface, both carry credentials in this untidy scenario.

watchPoints.text: If Time To Bite is allowed to bowl along in front without any challenge from Roaring Home or Porter In The Park before the home turn, the leader could prove very difficult to peg back over 2m6f on this good ground — monitor the pace being set after the first three hurdles.

Juan Bermudez is a natural prominent racer who may find himself shuffled back by Roaring Home, Porter In The Park, and Jackstell at the start — if he cannot secure his customary position his chance is materially compromised.

Notnowlinda returns after only 16 days; watch in the paddock and at the start for any signs of freshness or edginess — Harry Skelton will need her to settle quickly to get into this race from the hold-up position.

Porter In The Park has had 94 days off and the trainer's 14-day stat of 0/6 offers little confidence; watch for signs of lack of fitness in the latter stages of the race if she races prominently throughout.
Dinons has his best form on soft or heavy ground and today's good surface is likely to find him out — watch for him to be ridden conservatively by Nathan Moscrop with winning prospects limited.

races.name: Envesca Safety Champions Handicap Steeple Chase

runners_data.name: Huckleberry Sting
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (three wins in last five, all on Good), stays 2m6f well with a sim-going record of 9/12, but a pure hold-up style over a trip where the finish can compress means it depends on the race truly falling apart late; Jack Andrews rides.|Premier Fantasy|Has course-specific Good-ground form (5/5 similar going), placed twice at this trip in recent starts, but the hold-up style and a 9-day turnaround with tongue-strap are factors; Nick Scholfield's yard is in decent form (3/16 T14) which is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Huckleberry Sting arrives on the back of a win last time out, and his recent sequence of two wins and two seconds in his last five starts marks him as a consistent and in-form threat; the chief concern is a demanding 168 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Premier Fantasy
runners_data.comment: Premier Fantasy arrives here in cracking nick, placed at each of his last two starts including a runner-up effort nine days ago, and he has run over today's trip and going before. Carrying 168 lb is the one query, but the overall profile makes him a confident selection.

runners_data.name: A Dublin Job
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner who will force the pace from flag fall, but a form string of five successive finishes in the 5-6 range on Good ground makes it hard to see past its role as pace-setter rather than winner; Cameron Johnstone-Baker claims 7lb, which helps the weight but he is an apprentice handler at this type of venue.
runners_data.comment: Rated 103 and ranked top of the field, A Dublin Job arrives with experience of today's distance and going and 21 days between runs leaving him fresh; the main risk is that he has been winless in his last five starts, all of which ended fifth or sixth.

runners_data.name: Jack Doyen
runners_data.note: Won two of his last four completed runs and unseated in the other, all at around 2m-2m1f; stretching to 2m6½f is the key question, but his prominent style suits a contested gallop and Ben Case's yard is 0/6 in the last 14 days which is a minor concern.
runners_data.comment: Jack Doyen unseated last time out, which clouds an otherwise strong recent profile that includes a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, though a mark of 90 and 160 lb to carry are stiff tests.

runners_data.name: Danny's Friend
runners_data.note: Opened his account at 2m1f on Good ground 74 days ago, so freshness is a factor to monitor; Jack Tudor is a high-class booking and the Christian Williams yard has a good record with this type, but the step up in trip and the 74-day gap both need to be absorbed.
runners_data.comment: Danny's Friend has won twice in his last five starts, most recently, but that run came 74 days ago and he ranks last on our figures in an eleven-runner field, making him very difficult to fancy despite his going experience.

runners_data.name: On The Platform
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with headgear (p) who has a win at 2m4f on Good and Soft; 62 days off and a flat recent form figure of 5-5 suggest he needs things to fall right, but the Belinda Clarke yard carries no T14 concern (0/0) and he handles this trip.
runners_data.comment: On The Platform showed he can win with a success in his last five starts, but a pulled-up effort and a pair of fifths since cloud his profile; he has run over today's going before and a 62-day break leaves his current fitness open to question.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: True front-runner and the other half of the pace duel; an excellent sim-going record (14/15) and Sean Bowen in the saddle are significant positives, but a form string of 4F2434 over 2m tells its own story — finds a rival late; stepping up to 2m6½f could be the making or breaking of his chances.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Gone In Sixty nonetheless shows consistency with a second and a third in that sequence, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; 146 lb is a stiff ask, however, and he faces a battle to break through from seventh in the ratings.

runners_data.name: Keep Me Posted
runners_data.note: Fades in the finish according to the form record, and while naturally a deep hold-up type, the congestion at the rear of this field means Harry Bannister is unlikely to get him fully away from the early rush; the sim-going record is modest (0W0P) and the redistribution of his position further constrains his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with two pull-ups among them, Keep Me Posted faces a stiff task here, ranked ninth of eleven on our figures; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after just 17 days, are the only crumbs of comfort carrying 145 lb.

runners_data.name: Bahtiyar
runners_data.note: Consistent placed horse (0W6P on similar going) whose natural closer's profile is compromised here because there are too many true hold-up types for the map to absorb at the rear; Ben Poste will need a slice of luck to find clear daylight, and 55 days off adds an extra unknown.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, though a second three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement; Bahtiyar has experience over today's trip and going, but 55 days off and a return rank of eighth of eleven suggest he faces a stiff ask under 145 lb.

runners_data.name: Watchoutitscookie
runners_data.note: A prominent type on a consistent placed run of form (three thirds in five), handled Good ground well (10/15 sim-going), and David Noonan is a capable claimer; lacks a win at this sort of level and the step to 2m6½f on this card is new territory, but he should stay honest through the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures, Watchoutitscookie faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a fresh eleven-day turnaround with a couple of recent thirds suggesting he can make the frame.

runners_data.name: Honneur De Sivola
runners_data.note: Returning from 165 days off — by far the longest layoff in the field — with two pulled-ups in recent starts and a genuinely hold-up style that will be squeezed further back than ideal by the redistribution; Brendan Powell riding but the question marks around fitness and form are substantial.
runners_data.comment: Two pulled-up efforts in his most recent starts make Honneur De Sivola hard to trust after 165 days off, yet a third in his last five starts and going experience give him fair claims on a mark of 69, with our rating of 86 suggesting he retains ability; the main risk is whether he returns fully wound up.

races.paceDynamic: A Dublin Job and Gone In Sixty are both confirmed front-runners who will battle for the lead from the off over this 2m6½f trip at Stratford on Good ground, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a procession. That honest, pressured pace across a stiff staying trip is likely to stretch the field early, suiting horses who can travel economically behind the leaders and produce a sustained late effort rather than a sudden burst. Jack Doyen and On The Platform, both prominent types, will look to sit just off the pace and benefit from the race being run at an honest tempo without burning too much fuel. The race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile — horses who settle in the slipstream of the duel, avoid early pressure, and stay on powerfully over the final fences; this field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, and Keep Me Posted, Bahtiyar, and Honneur De Sivola are genuine closers who are unlikely to secure their natural deep positions, meaning true off-the-pace tactics will be harder to execute than normal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalkers Win
scenarios.trigger: If A Dublin Job and Gone In Sixty burn each other off at a genuine gallop, leaving the race to a well-placed stalker coming through late fences.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners set a pressured, honest pace that drains their reserves over 2m6½f, handing the advantage to horses who have settled within striking distance from the second circuit onwards; the Good ground rewards those with class and stamina rather than pure speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters — most likely Gone In Sixty given stable form — dictates at a controlled tempo and the duel fizzles, allowing a front-runner to dictate and ration its effort.
scenarios.body: With the gallop less severe than anticipated, a front-runner can conserve enough energy to repel challengers at the final fences; Gone In Sixty's Good-ground profile (14/15 similar going) and Sean Bowen's experience make this the more credible front-running outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but even-paced rather than frantic, allowing a prominent horse to maintain rhythm and outlast rivals through the staying test.
scenarios.body: On The Platform and Jack Doyen can slot into a handy position behind the duel and simply grind past tiring leaders in the straight; their ability to race close to the speed without being embroiled in it is the key asset over this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners truly exhaust themselves and the race collapses in the final half-mile, opening a window for genuine hold-up horses to finish fastest.
scenarios.body: This shape is undermined by the redistribution of Keep Me Posted, Bahtiyar, and Honneur De Sivola — none will likely get the deep, off-the-pace position they need to produce a true late swoop; even if the pace collapses, these horses will be racing closer to the speed than suits them.

watchPoints.text: Watch A Dublin Job and Gone In Sixty's opening half-mile — if they immediately lock horns at a fierce clip, the race will likely be run to suit the stalkers (Jack Doyen, Danny's Friend) who can sit just off the carnage.
Jack Doyen's trip record is unproven beyond 2m1f; if he begins to struggle from three out, his prominent position could turn from asset to liability as the extra half-mile bites.
Honneur De Sivola is 165 days absent with two recent pull-ups — monitor at the early fences for any signs of jumping hesitancy that could signal the layoff has taken a toll.

Keep Me Posted carries the ⚠ fades-in-finish tag and will be racing closer to the speed than natural due to field congestion — watch whether Harry Bannister opts to push wider to find racing room rather than be hemmed in on the rail in the final circuit.

Danny's Friend has not run for 74 days; watch the pre-race paddock demeanour and how sharply Jack Tudor sends him into his jumping rhythm early — if he is rusty at the fences, the layoff becomes a live concern at this trip.

races.name: Andy Townsend Memorial Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Mistral Blue
runners_data.note: Stratford's lone front-runner with strong Good-ground form (sim-going 12/15, 3W6P) and a 17-day turnaround; apprentice Fern O'Brien (5) must control the tempo sensibly over 2m6f — rated highly for this shape but style-fit flag (0.92) and a wide-margin style difference from her natural prominent role warrants mild caution if the race asks a different question.
runners_data.comment: Mistral Blue landed a win three starts back and was third four starts back, giving her a lively recent profile, and with experience of today's distance and going she merits respect — though that unplaced effort last time is the clear caution.

runners_data.name: Leave Her To Me
runners_data.note: 51-day break is the key concern for a hold-up mare who wants to creep into this off a true gallop; trainer combination has a flat 0/4 run in the last 14 days, but three wins at similar going on record and genuine stamina for 2m6f make her a serious late threat if the race is run honestly.
runners_data.comment: Leave Her To Me landed a win in her last five starts and has experience of today's trip and conditions, giving her a solid each-way profile at 167 lb; the main concern is her consistency, having pulled up and finished sixth in her two most recent outings.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: A consistent placed performer (five runs, all top-three or close) on Good ground with an amateur rider (Miss Imogen Mathias, 7lb claimer) and headgear (visor) suggesting connections are trying to sharpen her finishing effort; 21 days since last run and 1W6P on similar going — ideally suited to a steady pace and clean run.
runners_data.comment: Consistent mare who has finished second or third in four of her last five starts, with today's trip and going presenting no unknowns; winless in recent starts but her place-form reads well, and 21 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh and ready.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a tidy second in her seasonal reappearance and consistent placed form (four fourth-place finishes) on Good ground; tongue-tie fitted, and J M Quinlan brings experience — zero wins on similar going across five attempts is a flag, but she handles the surface and the trip comfortably.
runners_data.comment: Blackwater Lilly rates highest of these ten on our figures and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid platform, but she carries a hefty 164 lb and remains winless in her last five starts, which is the concern.

runners_data.name: Lady Bee Great
runners_data.note: Recent back-to-back wins (form P3-118) give her strong current form but she naturally drifts back in the finish despite those wins — her hold-up tendency is real and a fading-in-the-finish warning is noted; 17 days since last run and Good ground suits (9/10 sim-going), though OR 94 means she needs everything to fall right at this level.
runners_data.comment: Lady Bee Great won two of her last five starts, including back-to-back victories two and three runs ago, but an eighth last time out clouds her credentials; she has experience of today's going, though 163 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Liasse d'Argent
runners_data.note: 98 days between runs is a significant freshness concern for a mare with no wins from four outings on similar going; a natural hold-up type at OR 81, the long absence and a 0W0P record on this surface make her a difficult proposition — STYLE_FIT 0.90 further tempers any enthusiasm if she cannot get her natural position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked ninth of ten on our figures, Liasse d'Argent faces a stiff task here, returning after 98 days off carrying 150 lb, though she does have experience of today's going.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent tracker behind Mistral Blue, which gives her a tactical role — she has two wins from 14 runs on similar ground and OR 80 is modest, but she should travel comfortably in second and could steal a place if the closers are caught in traffic off a slow tempo.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Quick Of The Night does at least bring going experience and a level of fitness after 21 days off, though carrying 149 lb and ranked seventh of ten on our rating leaves her with plenty to find from a midfield berth.

runners_data.name: Sadies Diamond
runners_data.note: Seven days between races is very tight, and the last-run gap is the headline concern; however, Sadies Diamond has placed form at this trip (3rd and 2nd in recent starts) and handles Good ground well (13/15) — a true hold-up type pushed into midfield on the map, her chance depends on traffic resolution rather than natural positioning.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Sadies Diamond faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's going before and her third two starts back shows she can hit the frame on her day.

runners_data.name: Porridge
runners_data.note: 88 days absent and a form string that ends P4-88P paints a challenging picture — no wins or places on Good or Soft in five outings and the long break makes fitness a genuine question; naturally suited to hold-up tactics but unable to secure that position in this traffic, making her the most speculative runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time and winless in her last five starts, Porridge faces an uphill task here, though she has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 89 suggests more ability than her mark of 75 implies; 88 days off is the remaining query.

runners_data.name: Mc'flo
runners_data.note: Five-year-old lightly raced for her age but the form string (8964P5) shows consistent mid-to-rear finishes; Brendan Powell rides and trainer has 0/3 in the last 14 days — she handles Good ground (10/13 sim-going) but OR 70 and an absence of any wins or placed efforts mark her as highly unlikely to trouble the front end of this race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, including a pulled-up effort, Mc'flo ranks bottom of our assessments and carries 142 lb, making her very hard to fancy; she does have experience over today's trip and going, and returns on a quick enough turnaround.

races.paceDynamic: Mistral Blue is the lone confirmed front-runner and will dictate from the outset at Stratford's 2m6f trip, setting a sustainable gallop on Good ground with no genuine pace rival to press or disrupt her. Quick Of The Night is the only other prominent-style runner and will track but is unlikely to force the issue, meaning the tempo is controlled entirely by Mistral Blue and her connections. This creates a single-file, even-paced scenario where the race is run to suit those who can travel economically in mid-division and produce a clean finish off a steady gallop. The race shape strongly favours hold-up types who can get a clear run and quicken late — particularly Parikarma, Leave Her To Me and Blackwater Lilly, who are genuine closers with the ability to exploit a steady pace set by one honest front-runner. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can honestly place at the rear; Lady Bee Great, Liasse d'Argent, Sadies Diamond, Porridge and Mc'flo are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning the pack behind Mistral Blue will be congested and positional scrimmaging is likely — those with the most tactical fluency and clean passages, most plausibly Parikarma and Leave Her To Me, are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mistral Blue Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Mistral Blue is allowed to bowl along at her own pace and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap off a comfortable gallop.
scenarios.body: Mistral Blue sets a moderate, uncontested tempo around Stratford's turns, conserves energy, and proves far harder to peg back than the big field might suggest when they finally launch their challenges; the prominent style is rewarded here with first run and a first crack at the last few hurdles.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is truly honest enough to string the field out and closers get a clean passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: The congestion in the hold-up group resolves itself for one or two well-ridden finishers who thread through in the Stratford straight; Parikarma's consistent placed form on Good ground and Leave Her To Me's stamina over this type of trip make them the most dangerous late challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmage Aids One
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses cause traffic issues that benefit the one runner who finds a gap earliest.
scenarios.body: With five natural hold-up types all forced into a mid-division cluster, a horse finding clear air first in the final turn could steal a decisive advantage; Blackwater Lilly, suited by the Good ground and with a consistent placed profile, and Sadies Diamond, fresh on seven days' rest, are best positioned to exploit a gap if it materialises.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart In Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Mistral Blue is headed early, creating an erratic gallop that suits an opportunist off a moderate pace.
scenarios.body: An uneven rhythm through Stratford's undulations unsettles the closers' timing and rewards a horse that has quietly crept into contention unnoticed; this is a low-probability shape but Lady Bee Great's recent winning form and ability to race handily, despite her hold-up tag, makes her a beneficiary if the race falls into disarray.

watchPoints.text: Mistral Blue's tempo control is the axis of this race — if Fern O'Brien (5) allows the gallop to slow significantly through the middle miles, the hold-up pack will arrive at the last hurdle in a wall, making the outcome highly unpredictable.

The five redistributed hold-up types (Lady Bee Great, Liasse d'Argent, Sadies Diamond, Porridge, Mc'flo) will all be competing for the same space in a congested mid-division — watch for interference between the third and final hurdles as they seek runs that may not materialise.

Leave Her To Me returns from 51 days off for a dual-trainer yard with a poor 14-day record (0/4); if she is short of peak fitness, her late challenge will simply not arrive in time despite the style being ideal for this race shape.

Parikarma's amateur rider Miss Imogen Mathias (7lb claimer) takes off significant weight on a horse already handicapped at OR 96 — positional decisions in a 10-runner field at Stratford will be critical and worth watching early to see if she secures a clear path.

Quick Of The Night (OR 80) is the only horse capable of applying any pressure to Mistral Blue in the early stages — if she pushes forward and closes the gap, even briefly, it could materially change the pace shape and open the race up to the hold-up runners sooner than expected.
